transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-22
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortega (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzales (Helix Product), Sam Patel (Helix ML Eng), Riley Fox (Helix CTO)
---
Summary:
Quick demo/walkthrough of Redwood's Eval & Quality Monitoring features in Console + API + Optimize recommendations. Focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons for a POC. Discussed integration points, alerting destinations, and pilot success criteria.
Topics:
- Prompt set creation and management
- Regression alerts and thresholds
- A/B comparisons and canary rollouts tied to eval metrics
- API vs Console flows for batch evals
- Security/SSO and private deployment concerns
---
[00:00] Avery: okay everyone can hear me?
[00:02] Maria: yes loud and clear, thanks for setting this up.
[00:08] Avery: great, I'm Avery, AE at Redwood, with Ben our SE. Today we'll run through the Eval and Quality Monitoring demo, show how prompt sets work, how you can get regression alerts when model outputs change, and how to do A/B comparisons tied to rollouts.
[00:25] Riley: high level that sounds good. we're mainly evaluating for a customer-facing summarization feature, want to make sure we don't regress on factuality and tone.
[00:33] Ben: cool, thanks. one thing up front, what are your current success metrics for the summarizer? is it ROUGE, human rating, or embedding-similarity?
[00:42] Sam: we're using a mix — automated embedding-sim for semantic similarity plus human acceptability score. also tracking hallucination counts when facts are contradicted.
[00:53] Avery: perfect, that's exactly the kind of hybrid metric we support. i'll share my screen — apologies if the screen share quality is a bit laggy.
[01:10] [screen share starts]
[01:15] Ben: ok on the console homepage, you can see "Evals" in the left nav — that's the centralized place for prompt sets and evaluation dashboards. note: some transcriptions abbreviate Redwood Optimize as just "Optimize" in UI — the console calls it "Evaluate & Monitor" in the left nav.
[01:30] Maria: quick question — can we import existing prompt sets? we have a bunch of legacy prompts in a spreadsheet.
[01:36] Ben: yes, you can either upload CSV or use the API to push prompt sets. i'll show both. we also support tagging prompts by intent and bucket so you can split by user cohorts.
[01:49] [02:10] Ben: here's an example prompt set for summarization — each row is prompt template, expected output, and an evaluation rubric. you can define multiple metrics per prompt: embedding similarity (cosine), BLEU/ROUGE if you want, and a custom predicate for hallucination detection.
[02:30] Sam: how does hallucination detection work? that's critical for us.
[02:34] Ben: good question — there are a couple patterns. one is rule-based checks (fact overlap, presence of named entities); another is embedding-based grounding where we compare model output embeddings to retrieved context embeddings and flag low similarity. we also have a built-in hallucination heuristic but you can plug in your own classifier. note: the transcript sometimes turns KV cache into K-V cash, so in docs it's K-V cache.
[03:00] Maria: neat. can alerts be tied to Slack and PagerDuty?
[03:05] Ben: yes — alerting destinations include Slack, email, webhook, and PD. you can set severity thresholds; for example, if mean-embedding-sim drops by >5% vs baseline or human-acceptability falls below .85 over a rolling 24h, you get an alert.
[03:26] Riley: is there throttling or noise control? we don't want to get spammed with small blips.
[03:31] Avery: absolutely — you can configure suppression windows, minimum delta thresholds, and group-level alerts. we also support composite rules: AND/OR across metrics to avoid noisy alerts.
[03:45] [04:10] Ben: switching to A/B comparisons — you can create experiments that split traffic between model A (e.g., gpt-like-open) and model B (quantized variant); Redwood will run evaluations on a randomized sample and build a leaderboard by your chosen metrics.
[04:30] Sam: do you store the raw outputs? for debugging we need to see exact output + context.
[04:35] Ben: yes, with configurable retention. for hosted customers default retention is 30 days; for Dedicated you can set retention via policy or push to your S3. in private deployments everything stays in VPC.
[04:52] Maria: any SOC2/ISO concerns with storing user content?
[04:56] Avery: we have SOC 2 Type II — we can share security docs. for PII you can opt-out of storing outputs or use on-prem. we'll attach the security pack after this call.
[05:10] Riley: good. back to metrics — how do we do head-to-head A/B: do you do significance testing?
[05:18] Ben: yes, we provide basic statistical tests (bootstrap confidence intervals) and a bayesian sign test option. we surface p-values, uplift, and a visualization for sample size needed.
[05:30] [06:00] Ben: demo: create a new Eval job, select prompt set "Summarize-Helix-Q1", pick metrics: emb_cosine, human_acceptability, hallucination_rate. choose baseline model "redwood-xxl-v1" and candidate "quant-xxl-v1". set sample size 2k, and schedule — immediate or nightly batch.
[06:28] Sam: for nightly batch can we use our test harness? we'd like to run nightly evals with our synthetic data.
[06:33] Ben: yep you can push batches via API: /v1/evals/batches. there's also an S3 import connector.
[06:40] Maria: if we see a regression after a rollout, can we auto-roll back?
[06:45] Avery: there are two patterns — 1) canary guardrails: during rollout Redwood monitors chosen eval metrics in real-time and can automatically pause or shift traffic back to the previous variant if thresholds are breached; 2) alert+manual rollback. auto-rollback requires Dedicated or private with your routing policy enabled.
[07:05] Riley: what's the latency impact for real-time eval checks? we can't add hundreds of ms.
[07:11] Ben: fair — the evals used for canary are lightweight samplings and usually use async checks; they don't add request latency for end-user calls. for synchronous checks you'd expect added latency and we don't recommend for production path.
[07:30] [08:00] Avery: quick aside — Optimize suggestions: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching/quant profiles and a quantization mode compatible with your workload to reduce cost while preserving eval scores. for example, quant-xxl-8bit gave ~2x cost reduction with <1% drop on embedding-sim for one customer.
[08:22] Sam: have you measured hallucination impact with quantization? sometimes quant increases fabrication.
[08:28] Ben: depends on model and dataset — Optimize runs prior evals and recommends profiles that minimize regressions on your chosen metrics. you can opt to lock to profiles that are validated against your prompt set.
[08:45] [09:15] Maria: can we do targeted prompt-set splits by user cohort? we want different thresholds for internal vs external customers.
[09:20] Ben: yes, prompt sets can be tagged with cohort and you can create separate eval jobs per cohort with different thresholds and alerting rules.
[09:31] Riley: also curious about A/B exposure on mobile vs web, need region-based routing.
[09:36] Avery: smart routing supports region and tier-based splits; rollout policies can be scoped to route or region.
[09:45] [10:05] Ben: showing the regression alert UI now — here's an alert card: metric, delta, baseline value, current window, sample count, links to failing examples, and quick actions: open ticket, mute, or create RCA.
[10:25] Maria: the failing examples are super helpful, can we annotate them with human feedback?
[10:30] Ben: yes — you can annotate, flag for retrain, or add to a prompt blacklist. annotations flow into the Eval history and can be exported.
[10:40] [11:00] Sam: for the POC we likely want a nightly batch eval + a canary rollout with auto-pause. what's the recommended sample size to catch a 5% drop?
[11:08] Ben: for 5% relative drop on embedding-sim with sd ~0.2 you'd want roughly 1k-2k samples; our planner will compute exact numbers based on your historical variance.
[11:20] Riley: okay good. questions on integration: we will likely use Redwood hosted for the eval features but run inference on our Dedicated GPUs. is that supported?
[11:30] Avery: yes, that's a common pattern — control plane hosted, inference on Dedicated or private. Eval batch jobs can be routed to Dedicated pools and logs/outputs stay in your tenancy.
[11:44] Maria: any gotchas with data residency? some EU customers require outputs stay in-region.
[11:49] Ben: we support region pinning and VPC-only retention for Private. we'll note it in the security pack.
[11:58] [12:30] Ben: walking through the API example now — POST /v1/evals with body: {prompt_set_id, metrics: ["emb_cosine","human_accept"], baseline_model, candidate_model, sample_size, schedule}. example payload is in the docs link i just pasted in chat: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/evals (link)
[12:55] Maria: can we run an ad-hoc A/B without affecting live traffic? just dry-run?
[13:00] Ben: yes dry-run mode is available — it will sample from a saved corpus or synthetic data you upload; no traffic is touched.
[13:12] Sam: whats the cost for repeated evals? we want nightly runs but cost matters.
[13:18] Avery: evals are priced by tokens processed and compute used; our Optimize tool can estimate cost impact and suggest smaller sample sizes or focused prompt subsets to reduce cost. we'll include a cost estimate in the benchmark sheet.
[13:35] [14:00] Riley: ok last set of security questions: SSO/SAML, RBAC for evals, and KMS integration for outputs?
[14:07] Ben: SAML SSO and RBAC are supported; you can restrict who can see failing examples. KMS/HSM integration for encryption at rest is supported for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys but we also offer bring-your-own-key for enterprise.
[14:30] Maria: perfect.
[14:35] Avery: quick recap and next steps — we'll send the benchmark template and the security pack, Ben will prepare sample alert configs, Sam will upload prompt sets, and we'll reconvene for a POC kickoff.
[14:50] Riley: sounds good, thanks.
[14:55] Maria: thanks everyone.
[15:00] [screen share ends]
